known.title: The plan deletes the contract's Linked branch timing subsection on the false premise that it only repeats the timing, which removes the only yolo dirty-checkout procedure.
known.locator: Research, contract bullet, Decision (line 11); Steps, row 1 contract_timing, Task (line 22)
known.summary: The decision says the new table row carries the timing, so the `### Linked branch timing` subsection 'only repeats it' and goes. At repo_ref that subsection (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md lines 372-385) holds more than the timing: the rule that the status stays `drafting`, the clean-checkout path through Linked branch items 1 and 3 to 5, and the only dirty-checkout commands (`gh issue develop` without `--checkout`, list again, `git fetch origin <branch>`, `git worktree add` at the `agent-worktrees/<repository-name>/issue-<n>` path), plus `Do all later work in that worktree. Keep its path out of durable records.` The table row `Dirty checkout at linked-branch setup | A separate clean worktree, without a question` (line 341) and the yolo skill's Draft step 5 `Set up the linked branch now, as the contract's Yolo runs section says.` (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/yolo/SKILL.md line 83) depend on those commands. Linked branch item 4 (plan-contract.md line 275) uses `--checkout` in the current checkout, so it is not a replacement. Effect: after step 1, a yolo run on a dirty checkout has no defined worktree procedure, location rule, or path-privacy rule, and the new intro pointer names a worktree rule that has no commands.

known.title: The plan says that `closedByPullRequestsReferences` lists only open pull requests whose head is the issue's linked branch, but GitHub lists every open pull request that links the issue, from any branch or repository.
known.locator: Research, yolo recovery bullet (line 12); Steps, row 2 yolo_recovery (line 23)
known.summary: The GitHub GraphQL reference (https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/issues, Issue.closedByPullRequestsReferences) defines the field as 'List of open pull requests referenced from this issue', with `excludeUserLinked` and `userLinkedOnly` arguments, so manually linked pull requests are in the default result. GitHub's linking documentation (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue) says that a closing keyword in any pull request description links that pull request to the issue, also from a different repository (`KEYWORD OWNER/REPOSITORY#ISSUE-NUMBER`), and that the sidebar can link one manually. The gh CLI (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_issue_view; query in https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/trunk/api/query_builder.go) requests `closedByPullRequestsReferences(first: 100)` with no head filter. No source limits the field to the linked branch. Effect: when another open pull request links the issue, the recovery that reads 'the pull request number from that field' can take a foreign pull request and resume the run on its head branch, so later commits and pushes go to the wrong branch.

known.title: The gate step's Files cell names only the yolo SKILL.md, but the content-hash backfill also rewrites plan-manager/SKILL.md because its hash covers the edited plan-contract.md reference.
known.summary: scripts/skills/content-hash.mjs at repo_ref hashes SKILL.md plus sorted references/*.md (comment at line 5; hashSkill at lines 73-89, reference bytes added at line 85). Step 1 edits plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md, so the plan-manager skill hash changes and `--backfill plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills` writes `content_hash` (and `metadata.updated` when it differs) into plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/SKILL.md (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/AGENTS.md lines 23-32). A scratch run of content-hash.mjs from repo_ref gave the stored hash 39f14e11... before a contract edit and `would-bump productivity/plan-manager (content changed)` after it; the landed change for this plan (commit 6e6d583) changed that SKILL.md content_hash line. That path is in no Files cell (row 1 names only plan-contract.md, row 3 names only yolo/SKILL.md), and plan-contract.md says `Files` defines scope (line 70). Effect: the required backfill write falls outside the step scope, so an implementer who keeps to Files leaves a stale hash and A1 and the plugin gate fail.

known.title: The release step says that release.mjs reverts its bump commit and deletes the tag on a red tag CI, but the script has pushed both and only prints recovery steps.
known.summary: In scripts/lib/plugin-release.mjs at repo_ref the release commits the bump (line 348), pushes it (line 349), and pushes the tag through `claude plugin tag --push` (line 353, IO at line 435) before it waits for tag CI. On a failed tag CI it prints 'NOT creating GitHub Release' and a recovery (line 364): bump the version again with `patch` (line 368) or move the tag by hand (lines 369-371), then throws (line 373). No path reverts the commit or deletes the tag; scripts/AGENTS.md line 157 says 'tag-CI fails  → exits non-zero, prints recovery', and root AGENTS.md line 110 forbids force-push or branch-destructive git operations without explicit user confirmation. Effect: after a red tag CI the 0.13.1 bump commit stays on main and the `plan-lifecycle--v0.13.1` tag stays on a red run; 'the same command' then bumps to 0.13.2, so the Done when 'Tag plan-lifecycle--v0.13.1 exists with green tag CI' can never be met through the stated recovery.
